messages.subject: CFA doubt
parts:
Hello all,
I'm a beginner in Lavaan, but please, let me make a question:
I have carried out a CFA by using the following syntax:

modelo4 <- 'Intrinseca =~ M1 + M6 + M11 + M16 
Identificada =~ M2 + M7 + M12 + M17
Introyectada =~ M3 + M8 + M13 + M18
Externa =~ M4 + M9 + M14 + M19
Desmotivacion =~ M5 + M10 + M15 + M20
Autonoma =~ Intrinseca + Identificada 
Controlada =~ Introyectada + Externa' 
fit <- cfa(modelo4, data = datos) 
summary(fit, fit.measures = TRUE, standardized=TRUE)

The results are shown in the following figure: 



In two cases, the regression weight is greater than 1 (with a negative variance). 

What could be wrong? and in any case, how could solve? 

Thank you very much.

messages.author: 99a06696c483481a
messages.subject: Re: CFA doubt
parts:
David--
     I think the primary issue is that statistical identification for your higher order factors is weak.  Each factor needs at least two dependents plus  a correlation with something else.  You are almost at the very minimum of this condition.  As a result, standard errors for the path estimates related to these higher order factors will be large, and confidence intervals will be wide.  It may be that the model is misspecified, but with parameter values just outside the acceptable range, I think that the weak identification is the more likely problem.
     If that is true, then you might address the problem by making the statistical identification more firm. That would mean either more dependents per factor, more correlates per factor, or (probably most effective) fewer free parameters.  If you have prior knowledge that would let you fix some of the parameter estimates to "known" values, then your other, free parameter estimates would become more stable, and you might obtain more acceptable estimates.
     You might also consider bootstrapping.  Perhaps if you re sample your data repeatedly, you will see that the mean values across replications are actually within the acceptable range.  That would be easy enough to set up and run.
--Ed Rigdon

On 07/07/2014 06:32 PM, Edward Rigdon wrote:
> You might also consider bootstrapping. Perhaps if you re sample
> your data repeatedly, you will see that the mean values across
> replications are actually within the acceptable range. That would be
> easy enough to set up and run.

Just try this:

fit <- cfa(modelo4, data = datos, se = "bootstrap", verbose = TRUE)
parameterEstimates(fit)

and you will get 95% bootstrap-based confidence intervals.

parts:
David--
     These results are not standardized.  Notice that, for each factor with observed variable indicators, the first loading is fixed to 1.00.  This means that the variance of the factor is being scaled based on the variance of the indicator--it is not standardized.  You can also see this by looking at the variances of Desmotivacion, Autonoma and Controlada.  These factors are not dependent on anything, so the "variances" listed in the results are the factors' total variances, and the values are not 1.0.  If you ask specifically for standardized results, then I think you will find that there is no problem in the second order factor Loadings.

--Ed Rigdon

2014-07-08 12:46 GMT+01:00 Edward Rigdon <edward...@gmail.com>:

David--
     These results are not standardized.  Notice that, for each factor with observed variable indicators, the first loading is fixed to 1.00.  This means that the variance of the factor is being scaled based on the variance of the indicator--it is not standardized.  You can also see this by looking at the variances of Desmotivacion, Autonoma and Controlada.  These factors are not dependent on anything, so the "variances" listed in the results are the factors' total variances, and the values are not 1.0.  If you ask specifically for standardized results, then I think you will find that there is no problem in the second order factor Loadings.
--Ed Rigdon

On 07/07/2014 06:32 PM, Edward Rigdon wrote:

      You might also consider bootstrapping.  Perhaps if you re sample
your data repeatedly, you will see that the mean values across
replications are actually within the acceptable range.  That would be
easy enough to set up and run.

Just try this:

fit <- cfa(modelo4, data = datos, se = "bootstrap", verbose = TRUE)
parameterEstimates(fit)

and you will get 95% bootstrap-based confidence intervals.

Yves.
